evidence.loc: 4.4 Star Formation Rates and Stellar Masses
evidence.quote: Note that the stellar masses of DSFGs are often highly uncertain, though not necessarily systematically so

referee_caveats_inferred: Only 18 sources (7 new), selected for a wide lambda_peak range; correlation 'sigma' values depend on an undescribed fit and significance estimator
Sigma_IR and lambda_peak both come from the same SED fit and share L_IR, so errors are correlated and part of the correlation may be built in
Sizes are mass-weighted RJ-tail sizes (and optically thick for z > 3 sources) used as proxy for the SFR-weighted size
Fixed tau = 1 at 200 um and fixed mid-IR slope drive lambda_peak and L_IR; the paper's own opacity check shows lambda(tau=1) varies 10-300 um
Mixed ALMA datasets (new data and ALESS data from another program) with different depths and different uv coverage; compact-only vs combined imaging differences not quantified

missing_for_reproduction: Calibration recipe, flux calibrator and flux-scale uncertainty
Full CLEAN parameters (image size, cell size, threshold, masks, spws)
SED input photometry and fit uncertainties for every source
Regression and significance method for the quoted relations
Stellar masses and ALESS measurements must be taken from other papers
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Two Band 7 configurations (C36-3 and C36-6) of continuum data for 7 targets, probably tens of GB of raw data (inferred guess)
reproducibility.score_reason: One public-style ALMA project code, imaging choices partly stated (robust, software version, aperture method), and a numeric table of fluxes and sizes; but calibration, SED photometry and regression details are missing, and ALESS and stellar-mass inputs come from other papers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The paper does not state that the data are public, and the SED photometry and fit/significance procedures needed for the main correlation results are not given in enough detail to redo them.

methods_papers.why: SED fitting technique used for lambda_peak and L_IR
Flux-density method and ALESS sizes measured the same way

companion_papers.why: COSMOS SCUBA-2 sample, spectroscopic redshifts and COSMOS stellar masses
z = 4.61 confirmation and two-component nature of 450.03
